atlas-se.0068: Graduates do well (91.1% of recent graduates in work), but youth unemployment is high at 24.3%: the gap falls on people without a degree or a network.
atlas-se.0069: The big programmes open in the first months of the year for an autumn start, and many students apply in their final year rather than waiting for graduation. Examples: SEB’s intake closed on 11 January 2026, Swedbank’s opens again in January 2027, and the Ministry of Finance recruits in spring 2027.
atlas-se.0070: Outside the programmes, recruitment can take several weeks or months to review, employers do not always tell unsuccessful candidates, and hiring slows in July.
atlas-se.0071: Business graduates of the Stockholm School of Economics sign early: of its 2025 master’s class 40% went into consulting and 29% into finance, over 60% started in Sweden and 38% of its international graduates stayed.
atlas-se.0072: KTH and Chalmers are the main feeders for engineering and IT; KTH’s Armada is described as Scandinavia’s biggest career fair, and Chalmers runs career services with workshops, drop-in sessions and one-to-one advice.
atlas-se.0073: UHR, the Swedish ENIC-NARIC office, offers an assessment tool that gives a PDF comparing your education with Swedish education, which you can send to an employer; employers may not know a foreign university, so explain what you can do.
atlas-se.0074: KTH lists 15 career fairs, and Armada, first on the list, is described as Scandinavia’s biggest career fair.
atlas-se.0075: ARKAD at Lund University’s LTH takes place over two days in November with about 200 companies; LTH also holds a Career Day for international students (21 April 2026) on CV writing, job search in Sweden and work permits.
atlas-se.0076: Stockholm University runs the Stockholm Student Academy, six evening sessions on Swedish society, culture and professional life, starting again in autumn 2026.
atlas-se.0077: Banks recruit through trainee programmes with winter windows: SEB’s international trainee programme takes graduates of the last two years every other year, and Swedbank’s analyst programme (over 10 months) reopens in January 2027 for recent graduates in industrial economics, mathematics, economics, statistics or computer science. SSE sent 29% of its 2025 class into finance.
atlas-se.0078: Handelsbanken lists several programmes for students and takes open applications for thesis and internships, contacting candidates when it sees a match; its summer jobs are advertised in the spring term.
atlas-se.0079: The Big Four have large Swedish practices (EY has about 2,700 staff across 50 offices) and recruit graduates for August starts, including into technology consulting in Stockholm, Gothenburg and Malmö.
atlas-se.0080: Consulting took 40% and finance 29% of SSE’s 2025 class; McKinsey, BCG, Bain and the Big Four recruit on campus.
atlas-se.0081: Industrial and consumer groups run trainee programmes that open from January to March for an August or September start; Lantmännen’s Graduate Trainee Program, which rotates new graduates through the business, came second among social-science students in Karriärföretagen’s 2026 student poll.
atlas-se.0082: Volvo Group’s graduate programmes (Finance, 12 months, next recruitment in autumn 2027; Purchasing, Operations and Engineering, 15 months) are found by searching “Graduate” on its job site.
atlas-se.0083: The Ministry of Finance’s nine-month trainee programme gives recent graduates a permanent post from the start, with visits to government agencies and EU institutions; the Government Offices’ internships of about 20 weeks are advertised in March and April and in September and October, are unpaid and include a security vetting for final candidates.
atlas-se.0084: IT recruitment has slowed but stays strong, with an estimated shortage of about 18,000 professionals a year to 2028, mostly in AI, software and cybersecurity; at the same time Ericsson has cut thousands of Swedish jobs and Malmö’s games studios shed junior generalists. KTH and Chalmers are the main feeders.
atlas-se.0085: Volvo Group’s Purchasing, Operations and Engineering programme suits people interested in IT and engineering; Academic Work places many graduates in IT and technology roles as consultants or direct hires.
atlas-se.0086: Large employers open trainee applications in the first months of the year for an autumn start; SEB’s closed on 11 January 2026, Swedbank’s reopens in January 2027 and the Ministry of Finance recruits in spring 2027. Ordinary vacancies are posted all year, slowing in July.
atlas-se.0087: The business-school pipeline is a master’s (80% of SSE’s class signed before graduating), but the programmes read name recent graduates without stating a degree level.
atlas-se.0088: UHR, Sweden’s ENIC-NARIC office, assesses foreign qualifications for people seeking work and for employers, and its tool gives a PDF to send to an employer; for regulated professions it points to the authority responsible.
atlas-se.0089: The top business school’s graduates sign early and KTH and Chalmers feed engineering, but the programmes read name no list of schools.
atlas-se.0090: Students work part-time in the bank or firm alongside the degree (Handelsbanken), write the thesis with a company, or intern; there is no formal dual-study degree for business or computing graduates in the sources read.
atlas-se.0091: The state offers a few graduate entries, such as the Ministry of Finance’s nine-month trainee programme and the Government Offices’ unpaid internships, but the large graduate programmes are in banks and industrial groups.
atlas-se.0092: A work permit needs the job advertised in Sweden and the EU/EEA and Switzerland for at least ten days, pay at least on par with collective agreements and at least 90% of the median salary (SEK 34,470 a month from 1 June 2026). See Visas for the rules.
atlas-se.0093: Many Swedish CVs carry a photo but it is not necessary; leave off the date of birth early in your career. Address the letter informally, by first name.
atlas-se.0094: A Swedish CV is no more than two pages, and one is better; reverse chronological, no superlatives (“lagom”), and gaps such as parental leave are accepted.
atlas-se.0095: The application includes a concise cover letter on why you suit the job and what you offer, not a repeat of the CV; it is usually in English with a note on your Swedish level, or in Swedish if the ad is.
atlas-se.0096: Employers often ask for references before a final offer; do not list them on the CV but provide them when requested.
atlas-se.0097: The sources read ask for a CV and letter; a UHR assessment PDF is the document to send when a foreign qualification is unfamiliar, and no source read asks for certified copies.
atlas-se.0098: There is no statutory minimum wage and pay is set by collective agreements; when you name a figure, say it is flexible and negotiate benefits such as extra holiday. Offers are usually quoted gross.
atlas-se.0099: References are checked for candidates who advance, and the Government Offices add a security vetting with an in-person interview for final candidates; no private-sector page read describes other checks.
atlas-se.0100: Stockholm University says many jobs are filled through networking, while Expat.com says most vacancies are advertised online; both a posted application and a warm contact work.
atlas-se.0101: Initial interviews are often remote, a CV in English is accepted unless you are truly comfortable in Swedish, and Invest in Gothenburg points to a job portal that filters English-speaking jobs; some trainee roles still require Swedish.
atlas-se.0102: Applications in English are accepted at many firms, but specific roles at SEB and most local employers need Swedish; only 38% of SSE’s international graduates work in Sweden. English is widely used in international workplaces, but Swedish is an advantage and in many roles a requirement.
atlas-se.0103: A typical process starts with a screening call, followed by one or two interviews and sometimes a test or case assignment; initial interviews are often remote, and processes can move quickly once they begin.
atlas-se.0104: Employers assess cultural fit and look for people who work well in a collaborative, egalitarian environment; punctuality and preparation are valued. Dress is mostly smart casual, formal mainly in law and finance.
atlas-se.0105: Programmes add steps: the Government Offices’ internship has an interview, reference checks and a security vetting with an in-person interview at the Government Offices in central Stockholm. Reviews can take weeks or months and unsuccessful candidates are not always told.
atlas-se.0106: Standard Swedish contracts run until further notice; an employer may add a probationary period of up to six months, which either side can end during it (an employer gives at least two weeks’ notice) and which becomes permanent if no one ends it.
atlas-se.0107: Special fixed-term employment is limited to 12 months within five years before it converts to permanent; collective agreements regulate wages, working time, pensions and notice periods beyond the statutory minimums.
atlas-se.0108: There is no statutory minimum wage: the average is roughly SEK 40,000 to 42,000 a month before tax, and offers are quoted gross, so use the Tax Agency’s calculator for net pay.
atlas-se.0109: The Ministry of Finance’s nine-month trainee programme comes with a permanent post from the start; you can name a flexible figure and ask what the company offers beyond salary.
atlas-se.0110: The employer must advertise the vacancy in Sweden and within the EU/EEA and Switzerland for at least ten days, simplest on Arbetsförmedlingen’s portal, whose ads also appear on EURES.
atlas-se.0111: Terms and pay must be at least on par with Swedish collective agreements and, from 1 June 2026, at least 90% of the median salary: SEK 34,470 a month, from a median of SEK 38,300 published on 16 June 2026.
